h: Bees, Vimto and a bit of jungle
p: Keep your eyes open around Manchester and you'll spot the worker bee everywhere: on bins, bollards, murals and mosaics. It's the city's symbol, a nod to its hard-working industrial past, and spotting them makes a fun little game for kids on the walk to and from your round. Another fact for the scorecard break: Vimto was invented in Manchester back in 1908.

As for the golf, a typical round takes about an hour. If you're a big group, think about splitting into two smaller teams so the game keeps moving and nobody is left waiting. Booking a set time means you can plan around trains, meals and match days, and arriving a few minutes early lets everyone settle in before the first putt.

For more city-centre ideas, Manchester Museum on Oxford Road is great for families, with natural history displays and plenty to look at, and the Whitworth art gallery sits in its own park nearby. Chinatown, just off Portland Street, is a lovely spot to grab a meal, and Manchester Central Library in St Peter's Square is a striking round building that's well worth a peek inside.

With a bit more time, Heaton Park on the north side of the city is a huge green space and makes for a great afternoon in the fresh air. Football fans will want to check out tours at either the Etihad or Old Trafford, depending on which half of the city they support.
